messages:
jessica (support): FYI customer Acme Apps reporting sudden p99 latency spike on text-gen. They say they pinned region=us-west but traces show requests egressing to eu-west-1. Impacting multiple requests since ~03:40 UTC. Request ID: req_0a9f7c. Can SRE/runtime take a look? :warning:

raj (eng-sre): Can you paste the trace and a sample request curl? Also curious if their SDK is sending a region header or relying on our routing. Any recent routing changes rolled out near 03:30 UTC?

jessica (support): Trace snippet (redacted):
```
span 1: client->edge us-west-1 (x-client-region=us-west)
span 2: edge->routing-controlplane lookup -> returned pool: eu-west-1-fallback
span 3: edge->egress eu-west-1 (assigned by routing-controlplane)
span 4: runtime serve -> model-host eu-west-1
error: capacity_shortage -> fallback_pool selected
```
curl reproducer they used: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -H "x-region: us-west" -d '{"model":"rwd-llama-13b","prompt":"hi"}'`

oliver (eng-runtime): This looks like a control-plane mapping issue. We had a routing config rollout at 03:28 UTC that included a regex change for region tags. If the regex mismatches, the control plane defaults to fallback pools (eu-west-1) instead of the explicit zone. I'll pull the rollout logs.

deploy-bot: deploy event: routing-controlplane v7.2.3 -> v7.2.4 initiated at 2026-06-09T03:28:14Z by oliver (eng-runtime). Canary 10% completed.

raj (eng-sre): Ooh. oliver, do we have a quick way to test the routing-controlplane mapping locally? If it's regex-related, might be a config file that slipped. Also want the egress IPs so we can map to region. Jessica, can you ask Acme for a few raw request IDs (they gave req_0a9f7c) and the full trace with egress IP?

jessica (support): Sent them a note. Acme replied with two more IDs: req_0aa12d, req_0ab03f and included egress IPs 34.240.10.12 and 3.248.56.90. They confirmed adding x-region header didn't help initially.

raj (eng-sre): IPs map -> 34.240.10.12 = eu-west-1 egress. So control-plane returned eu-west despite client header. Quick mitigation: oliver, can we enable the experimental header override `x-redwood-force-region` on edge for customer org=acme to bypass control-plane decision? That would get them back to us-west.

oliver (eng-runtime): I can push a targeted policy in the control plane: if org==acme then honor `x-region` header and skip fallback decision. Pushing now to canary host group.

deploy-bot: policy update: targeted routing override for org=acme deployed to canary at 2026-06-09T03:41:02Z.

maria (customer): Confirmed — after the override our p99 dropped from 1.2s -> 180ms. Thanks. Using the header workaround for now.

raj (eng-sre): Good. Root cause hypothesis: v7.2.4 rollout introduced a faulty region-tag regex in routing rules that mis-classified some us-* tags as unmatched, causing fallback to eu-west pools. oliver, can you revert or patch? Also need a postmortem entry and notify support SLA escalation.

oliver (eng-runtime): Patch merged: tighten region regex to explicitly accept `^(us|eu|ap)-(west|east|central)(-[0-9]+)?$` and added unit test. Rolling v7.2.5 with fix. Reverting canary to 0% for v7.2.4.

deploy-bot: deploy event: routing-controlplane v7.2.5 deployed at 2026-06-09T03:57:00Z.

raj (eng-sre): Thanks. Next steps: 1) confirm full rollback for any impacted orgs (jessica to verify), 2) follow-up postmortem + alert for future regex changes, 3) add e2e test that simulates header/regex matches.

jessica (support): I'll reach out to Acme to confirm stability over next 24h and file the SLA incident. For tracker: INC-2026-314.

maria (customer): All good from our side — traffic normal and latency stable. Appreciate the quick turnaround. :heart:

raj (eng-sre): Closing here, but leaving the incident open for the postmortem. Root cause: routing-controlplane misconfiguration (regex) causing unexpected cross-region fallbacks. Mitigation: targeted header override + v7.2.5 patch.
